result.title: Memorization Lives in a Few Attention Heads: Mitigating Memorization in Diffusion Models via Projection-Based Suppression
result.summary: Diffusion models can memorize and reproduce training samples during inference, raising serious privacy and copyright concerns. Existing inference-time mitigation methods often suppress conditional information globally, which may reduce memorization but can also harm semantic alignment and image quality. In this paper, we revisit memorization from the perspective of cross-attention heads. Through systematic analysis and targeted ablation, we find that memorization is mainly driven by a small subset of shallow-layer attention heads with abnormally strong semantic control, rather than by the entire cross-attention mechanism. Motivated by this finding, we propose Projection-based Top-k Attention Head Suppression, a targeted inference-time mitigation method. Our method first identifies the top-k attention heads most related to memorization using a semantic-control score, and then removes their condition-specific components through directional projection between conditional and unconditional representations. This design selectively weakens memorization-related features while preserving useful semantic information. Extensive experiments on different diffusion models and datasets show that our method effectively reduces memorization and achieves a better trade-off between memorization mitigation and image quality than existing approaches.

AI.brief_summary: 该文发现扩散模型的训练样本记忆主要由少数浅层 cross-attention head 驱动，提出用语义控制分数选出 top-k head 并通过条件／无条件表示间的方向投影抑制其条件分量，从而在推理期减轻记忆同时保留语义与画质。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用打分定位稀疏 attention head、再以投影定向移除特定特征」的手法，可能可供核查为定位 VLM 中承载视觉证据或 latent 内容的少量头并做定向干预的线索，但研究对象是扩散图像生成，与 LVR 的状态生成和证据使用无直接联系。
